outcome.technical: ESTABLISHED FIRST, BY RUNNING: a scratch script built three plans in tempfile.mkdtemp (removed in finally), each resolving reviewSkill from one level (phase.reviewSkill / meta.areas.api.reviewSkill / meta.reviewSkill), and ran the working tree's plugins/audit/scripts/status/audit-lookup.py <plan> brief P1 --role phase --project <proj> at 0eeb2b7f: exit 0 all three, phase.md written (6423/6421/6421 bytes), the skill name in it False all three, and no line containing 'review skill' or 'reviewSkill'. So the bug was real; filed BUG-34-ukq (med) with the exported copy's audit-task.py bug-add against docs/audit/audit-plan.json - the orchestrator closes it at commit time. FIX: (1) plugins/audit/scripts/status/audit-lookup.py gains review_skill_lines(manifest, phase), called right after the rules line in phase_brief_parts' header (so every slice of a cut brief carries it): a '## Review skill' section with '- <skill> (basis: <basis>, ...)' exactly as _areas.resolve_review_skill returns them and an instruction to invoke it via the Skill tool FIRST; [] when no skill resolves, including an explicit null - no second precedence chain. (2) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py: session_skills(ctx, task, phase_review=False) appends the resolved review skill (deduped) when phase_review is set; writer_argv passes a new phase_review keyword through; validation_dispatch (the headless reviewer-role session over the phase review's findings) sets it. WHAT I FOUND ABOUT 'THE HEADLESS REVIEWER SESSION': the phase review itself on the drive route is an Agent dispatch (dispatch_phase_review -> dispatch_said, subagent audit-reviewer handed the brief path), not a writer_argv session - the brief section is what reaches it. The writer_argv sessions under role reviewer are the per-task reviewer (reviewer_dispatch, mode: task - agents/audit-reviewer.md:9 says that mode takes no review skill, and reference/execute-task.md:487 says not to pass one) and the validation session at phase scope. The latter did not get the skill (vk1 red); it now does, and the per-task reviewer is pinned not to (vk3). TESTS: tests/test_audit_lookup.py new rk-block (_review_skill_brief_cases, staged in _selftest): rk1-rk3 each level set beside a lower level carrying a DIFFERENT name, asserting one heading, the skill on exactly one body line with 'basis: <what the resolver returned>', and no other level's name anywhere in the brief; rk4 no skill anywhere -> written brief, no section; rk5 area reviewSkill null with meta set -> no section, plan skill never named. tests/test_drive_phase.py: _review_skill_session_units called from _skill_units (uy-block): vk1 validation argv carries the area's review skill once and not the overridden plan one, role reviewer; vk2 none and an explicit phase null give no --skill; vk3 the per-task reviewer over a review-skill phase carries only the task's skills.
